label: Meshullam

text.BHSA NEH 8:3: וַיִּקְרָא־בֹו֩ לִפְנֵ֨י הָרְחֹ֜וב אֲשֶׁ֣ר׀ לִפְנֵ֣י שַֽׁעַר־הַמַּ֗יִם מִן־הָאֹור֙ עַד־מַחֲצִ֣ית הַיֹּ֔ום נֶ֛גֶד הָאֲנָשִׁ֥ים וְהַנָּשִׁ֖ים וְהַמְּבִינִ֑ים וְאָזְנֵ֥י כָל־הָעָ֖ם אֶל־סֵ֥פֶר הַתֹּורָֽה׃
text.KJV NEH 8:3: And he read therein before the street that was before the water gate from the morning until midday, before the men and the women, and those that could understand; and the ears of all the people were attentive unto the book of the law.
text.BHSA NEH 8:4: וַֽיַּעֲמֹ֞ד עֶזְרָ֣א הַסֹּפֵ֗ר עַֽל־מִגְדַּל־עֵץ֮ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשׂ֣וּ לַדָּבָר֒ וַיַּֽעֲמֹ֣ד אֶצְלֹ֡ו מַתִּתְיָ֡ה וְשֶׁ֡מַע וַ֠עֲנָיָה וְאוּרִיָּ֧ה וְחִלְקִיָּ֛ה וּמַעֲשֵׂיָ֖ה עַל־יְמִינֹ֑ו וּמִשְּׂמֹאלֹ֗ו פְּ֠דָיָה וּמִֽישָׁאֵ֧ל וּמַלְכִּיָּ֛ה וְחָשֻׁ֥ם וְחַשְׁבַּדָּ֖נָה זְכַרְיָ֥ה מְשֻׁלָּֽם׃ פ
text.KJV NEH 8:4: And Ezra the scribe stood upon a pulpit of wood, which they had made for the purpose; and beside him stood Mattithiah, and Shema, and Anaiah, and Urijah, and Hilkiah, and Maaseiah, on his right hand; and on his left hand, Pedaiah, and Mishael, and Malchiah, and Hashum, and Hashbadana, Zechariah, and Meshullam.
text.BHSA NEH 8:5: וַיִּפְתַּ֨ח עֶזְרָ֤א הַסֵּ֨פֶר֙ לְעֵינֵ֣י כָל־הָעָ֔ם כִּֽי־מֵעַ֥ל כָּל־הָעָ֖ם הָיָ֑ה וּכְפִתְחֹ֖ו עָֽמְד֥וּ כָל־הָעָֽם׃
text.KJV NEH 8:5: And Ezra opened the book in the sight of all the people; (for he was above all the people;) and when he opened it, all the people stood up:

A.name: Meshullam
A.line: stood at Ezra's left hand as he read the law to the people (NEH 8:4)
A.notes: The priest who sealed the covenant (NEH 10:7), the chief of the people who sealed it (NEH 10:20) and the head of the house of Ginnethon (NEH 12:16) are held apart; the text does not say whether any of them is this man.

B.name: Meshullam
B.line: Stood at Ezra's left hand when he read the law to the people
family: companion-of ezra (Ezra, son of Seraiah (EZR 7:1), scribe skilled in the Law (EZR 7:6)

why: מְשֻׁלָּם names one man, last in the list at Ezra’s left hand, matching A. B states the same identifying facts, so the passage cannot distinguish A from B; the choice is uncertain.
